developmentFixturePostflight.interpretation: Failed pilot left a nonempty queue without consumers. Preserved as failed postflight, then removed by exact owned fixture cleanup; excluded from final acceptance.

limits: Dense actions enter the actual durable Rabbit indexing queue; this does not measure SHIP action decoding throughput.
Actual genesis blocks traverse production master, reader, deserializer and indexer processes.

The bulk proxy gates forwarding of bulk requests before dispatch to Elasticsearch. Actual upstream responses remain unchanged after release; the controlled stall does not establish native Elasticsearch saturation or delayed post-ES acknowledgments.
Publisher confirms, proxy request-to-response timings (including any pre-dispatch gate), database receipt copies, and final physical-copy reads are distinct observations.
No true broker-delivery-to-Elasticsearch per-item acknowledgment latency was instrumented.
Profiling and observer overhead, distinct fresh fixtures, and other host workloads preclude runtime/capacity rankings.
Bounded recovery observations do not establish heap-leak freedom, production capacity, long-duration stability or full-chain replay acceptance.
The archived fixture password and producer key are known test-only credentials. Raw artifacts are not rewritten or sanitized.
